docs.x: PXD2 · floor Reform College · B.A. Civics Lex rex · the law is king A complete Bachelor of Arts. Four years, 120 credits. Built to compete with the education John Witherspoon gave at Princeton — languages, Euclid, moral philosophy, natural philosophy, Scripture, and the American founding — not to counterfeit the later research university. What this is. A finished undergraduate curriculum, reading list, examination standard, and lecture map. The lectures already live in this hall (Civics, Resistance, STEM) and in free courses we cite: Hillsdale, MIT OpenCourseWare, Open Yale. Primary texts are public domain. A student who finishes the map, sits the examinations, and defends the thesis has done a BA’s work. What this is not. A state-accredited diploma mill and not Princeton University. We do not sell a Princeton degree, use their seal, or pretend a bureau has blessed this. If PXD2 later charters a college, this catalog is the program. Until then it is an education, which is the thing Princeton was for when Witherspoon sat in Nassau Hall. From 1768 to 1794 Witherspoon’s College of New Jersey was not a graduate school with a souvenir undergraduate brand. It was a BA: Latin and Greek, mathematics, natural philosophy, and moral philosophy as the capstone — the same moral philosophy this hall already teaches from Knox, Rutherford, Craighead, and Witherspoon. That is the education we compete with. The later university added departments, professional schools, and a different theory of man. Reform College does not chase that. It restores the BA as a single course of study in which a graduate can read a statute, a demonstration, a psalm, and a constitution without a translator from the current system. “Civil liberty cannot be long preserved without virtue.” John Witherspoon — the Princeton we are answering, not the one that replaced him. Bachelor of Arts in the Reformed Liberal Arts. 120 semester credits. Eight terms. One language sequence through Greek or Hebrew after Latin. One concentration. Senior thesis in public. docs.x: PXD2 STUDIOS Status: Funding open · Concho, Arizona · 100% off-grid studio Unreal Engine · PC · Epic Games Store A modern war for the world's straits. Command a submarine, a mini frigate and FLIR-equipped drones in a combat game built by one developer in Arizona, from Blender models to Unreal. Back the game Follow the build REC · GAMEPLAY CAPTURE PXD2 // BUILD 0.x Gameplay trailer Real in-engine footage posting here soon 01 Situation US forces flying and sailing PXD2-designed systems face the Meridian Coalition's navy and air force for control of the chokepoints that move the world's shipping. The maps are naval-sim large. The action stays fast and readable, with clean explosions and destruction you fight through. Mud for Blood is the story campaign. It leads into online multiplayer on the same full-size maps, with community dedicated servers the way PC shooters used to run them. Hull 79 carrier · in-game model Subsurface Submarine Run silent. You can actually see the boat underwater. Surface Mini frigate Every system on the hull modeled and in the fight. Air Drones Toggle FLIR, infrared and other vision modes mid-mission. 02 Hero map A modern tunnel-warfare battlefield: close, dark, loud and unlike anything else in the genre. Above ground, long-range sniping rewards patience over twitch reflexes, so veteran players have a place to shine. More theaters in the current build: Battle for LA · Fight for Japan · Operation Iron Furrow · Bandar · Drone Hunter. Modes: Mud for Blood campaign, fleet battles, FPS, and Battle Royale with a B-52 drop and ram-air parachute. 03 The studio PXD2 is Chad Peters: software developer, PCB and embedded engineer, and solo game builder, working from a fully off-grid studio in Concho, Arizona. Every ship, sub and drone was modeled in Blender and brought into Unreal Engine. The first playable build came together in about a week, and early public gameplay drew a strong response. GLOBAL THEATERS is planned as a franchise. Vietnam and Global War on Terror titles follow, each kept focused, moddable and playable on ordinary PCs. 04 Precedent Military shooters and naval sims have been built this way before: crowdfunded first, then grown into hits. docs.x: PXD2 Hornet Bell Edu Ages 6–11 · militia cartoon · 5 min spoken A militia educational cartoon from the North Carolina Piedmont. Bell, Vee, and Lee say each story aloud for five minutes — records from Davidson, Chapel Hill, and Nassau Hall — so children can love the cousins, not the statues. Wilson daughters, Davidson, Graham father and son, Polk, Brevard, Adlai Osborne, Reese, Knox, Caldwell — then Washington, Madison, Jackson, Cousin Polk, Lincoln’s books. Open an episode and they speak. Mary Wilson married Ezekiel Polk (President James Knox Polk’s line). Violet Wilson married Major John Davidson. Joseph Graham married their Isabella. Ephraim Brevard and Adlai Osborne, cousins, Princeton 1768. Gen. William Lee Davidson fell at Cowan’s Ford; the Rural Hill horse came home. In this family the Davidsons are one house, not two: the general is uncle to Major John and to Adlai Osborne. Col. Thomas Polk was tasked to escort Philadelphia’s bells — including the Liberty Bell — to Allentown, arriving 24 September 1777, so they would not be melted for cannon. His son William , later Lt. Col., served in that same North Carolina line (Germantown, Guilford, Cowan’s Ford, Eutaw). Joseph Graham was first sheriff of Mecklenburg, N.C. senator, justice of the peace for decades, brigadier (1814) and major general of militia — not governor. His son William A. Graham was Governor of North Carolina (1845–49), U.S. Senator, Secretary of the Navy, and the 1852 Whig vice-presidential nominee. James Knox Polk sat in the White House from this same web. Local, bench, militia, state executive, president: one house. Open the live hall’s House tab for the full table. ← All episodes Quiet
